message.content:
Work in /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TS, live prod tree). You OWN the "app chrome" only: sidebars, top bars / headers, floating widgets, and the global search. Do NOT edit admin content pages (mail, chat, billing), lib/mailer, or the hosting wizard — other agents own those.

Implement these three board cards:

1. **Admin Portal Sidebar — hide agency & ads** (card cmsu3p8de): In the ADMIN portal sidebar/nav, hide the "Agency" and "Ads" navigation entries (the marketing-agency + ads-autopilot sections). Find the admin sidebar/nav config and remove/feature-flag those items so they don't show. Don't delete the pages, just hide the nav.

2. **Feedback & chatbot widgets in admin** (card cmst2pfmb): The marketing floating **Feedback** widget and the customer **live-chat** widget should NOT be visible in the ADMIN portal (they're for customers). Instead, in the admin portal add: (a) a **support/ticket** indicator widget and (b) an **email** indicator widget, and (c) when there's a new notification / new email / new ticket / new live-chat reply, show an **animation** (e.g. a notification bell with a badge/pulse). Reuse existing notification/unread data sources if present (there are admin unread endpoints like /api/admin/chat-unread). Screenshot(s) for this card may be at /opt/nxeon/board-uploads/board/cmst2pfmb00crhlxvzfys5o6s/ — read them with the Read tool if present.

3. **Better global search bar** (card cmsrlfza): The top-bar "Search anything" currently only searches pages, which is pointless. Make it a real command-palette style search that also finds **emails, hosting plans/accounts, websites, servers, domains, customers (admin)** and jumps straight to them. Add a search API route that queries those models (scoped correctly: customers search only their own; admins can search across) and wire the existing top-bar search UI to it with grouped results + keyboard nav. Keep it fast (debounced, limited results).

Constraints: do NOT run `npm run build`/`next build` (I integrate + build once) — verify with `npx tsc --noEmit` only. Match existing component/styling patterns. Report: files changed, what each does, tsc result, and anything ambiguous you had to decide.

1	/**
2	 * Information architecture for the admin ops portal.
3	 *
4	 * The sidebar shows one TOP-LEVEL ENTRY per destination cluster (14 of them,
5	 * across 5 sections). Every entry carries an icon and links to `tabs[0]`; its
6	 * remaining members are reached from a horizontal sub-tab bar rendered once by
7	 * the admin layout via <AdminSubTabs /> (see components/admin/SubTabs.tsx).
8	 *
9	 * That keeps all ~41 admin routes exactly two clicks away while the sidebar
10	 * stays short enough to fit a 1080p laptop with no scrolling — the previous
11	 * shapes (6 collapsed group headers, then 41 flat rows) failed at one end or
12	 * the other. No route was moved or removed: every URL that worked before still
13	 * resolves, it is simply reached through its parent entry's tab bar now.

308	/** Every entry across every section, in sidebar order. */
309	export function adminEntries(): AdminEntry[] {
310	  return ADMIN_NAV.flatMap((g) => g.entries);
311	}
312	
313	/**
314	 * Does `pathname` belong to `href`? Exact match, or a detail route beneath it
315	 * (`/admin/users/123`). The bare "/admin" only ever matches exactly so it can
316	 * never swallow every deeper route.
317	 */
318	export function hrefMatches(href: string, pathname: string): boolean {
319	  if (pathname === href) return true;
320	  if (href === "/admin") return false;
321	  return pathname.startsWith(href + "/");
322	}
323	
324	/**
325	 * Resolve which top-level entry owns a given admin pathname, by longest
326	 * matching member href. Returns null for admin paths outside the IA.
327	 */
328	export function entryForPath(pathname: string): AdminEntry | null {
329	  let best: { entry: AdminEntry; len: number } | null = null;
330	  for (const entry of adminEntries()) {
331	    for (const tab of entry.tabs) {
332	      if (hrefMatches(tab.href, pathname) && (!best || tab.href.length > best.len)) {
333	        best = { entry, len: tab.href.length };
334	      }
335	    }
336	  }
337	  return best?.entry ?? null;
338	}
